title: Length and Capacity: Comparing and Measuring
seo_title: Length and Capacity – Primary 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Compare lengths (long, short, tall) and capacities (full, empty, holds more, holds less); measure using hand spans, steps and cups. (summary of the NERDC Primary 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 1 maths worksheets on comparing length, height, weight and capacity, measuring with hand spans, steps and cups, and simple problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Line up the ends to compare
key_sub: Full holds the most; empty holds nothing.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To compare lengths, line up the ends. The one that sticks out more is longer.
  • We can measure with hand spans, steps, sticks or cubes.
  • A container that holds more water has a bigger capacity.

Examples

Example

A pencil is 6 cubes long; a crayon is 4 cubes long

6 is more than 4

Answer: The pencil is longer

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not lining up the endsStart at the same place.
Leaving gaps when measuringPut the units end to end.
Thinking tall means holds moreCheck by pouring.

items.q: Put them in order from longest to shortest.
items.e: Find the longest first: the straw. Then the next: the pencil. Last is the shortest: the eraser. So the order is straw, pencil, eraser.

items.q: The rope is longer than the stick. The stick is longer than the pencil. Which is the longest?
items.e: The rope is longer than the stick, and the stick is longer than the pencil. So the order is rope, stick, pencil. The rope is the longest.

items.q: The bus is longer than the car. The car is longer than the bike. Which is the shortest?
items.e: The order from longest is bus, car, bike. The bike is the shortest.

items.q: The ribbon is shorter than the yarn. The yarn is shorter than the rope. Which is the longest?
items.e: Each one is shorter than the next. From shortest: ribbon, yarn, rope. So the rope is the longest. Read “shorter” carefully.

items.q: The cat is shorter than the dog. The dog is shorter than the horse. Which animal is in the middle?
items.e: From shortest to tallest: cat, dog, horse. The dog is in the middle.

items.q: Ife is taller than Hauwa. Hauwa is taller than Aminat. Who is the shortest?
items.e: Ife is taller than Hauwa, and Hauwa is taller than Aminat. From tallest: Ife, Hauwa, Aminat. Aminat is the shortest.

items.q: Halima cannot move her desk to the door. She uses a string. The string is as long as the desk. The string is shorter than the door. Which is longer?
items.e: The string is the same length as the desk. The door is longer than the string, so the door is longer than the desk too. The door is longer.

items.q: Blessing has a string. It is as long as her book. The string is longer than her pencil. Which is longer, the book or the pencil?
items.e: The book and the string are the same length. The string is longer than the pencil. So the book is longer than the pencil.

items.q: The green snake is longer than the blue snake. The red snake is shorter than the blue snake. Which list goes from longest to shortest?
items.e: Green is longer than blue. Red is shorter than blue. So blue is in the middle: green, blue, red.

items.q: How many cubes long is the crayon?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the crayon to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Ruth lays cubes along her book, end to end, with no gaps. She uses 9 cubes. How long is the book?
items.e: Ruth used 9 cubes from one end of the book to the other. So the book is 9 cubes long.

items.q: Which is true?
c: The orange is heavier than 4 cubes.
The orange is lighter than 4 cubes.
The orange weighs the same as 4 cubes.
items.e: The orange side goes down. The side that goes down is heavier. So the orange is heavier than 4 cubes.

items.q: Which is true?
c: The feather weighs the same as 2 cubes.
The feather is heavier than 2 cubes.
The feather is lighter than 2 cubes.
items.e: The feather side goes up. The side that goes up is lighter. So the feather is lighter than 2 cubes.

items.q: A brick and a sponge are on a balance. The brick is heavier. Which side goes down?
items.e: The heavier thing makes its side go down. The brick is heavier, so the brick side goes down.

items.q: Victor thinks the beach ball is heavier because it is bigger. On the balance, the beach ball side goes up. Is Victor right?
items.e: The side that goes up is lighter. So the beach ball is lighter. Victor is not right. Big things can be light.

items.q: The melon is heavier than the apple. The apple is heavier than the grape. Which is the lightest?
items.e: From heaviest to lightest: melon, apple, grape. The grape is the lightest.

items.q: The tin is lighter than the bag. The bag is lighter than the box. Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Each one is lighter than the next. From lightest: tin, bag, box. So the box is the heaviest. Read “lighter” carefully.

items.q: How full is the glass?

items.q: How full is the glass?
items.e: Split the glass into 4 equal parts. The water fills 1 part. It is quarter full. Half full would reach the middle.

items.q: How full is the jar?
items.e: The water is close to the top, but not right at the top. The jar is nearly full.

items.q: How full is the jar?
items.e: The water comes up to the middle. Half is water and half is empty. The jar is half full, not nearly full.

items.q: How full is the jar?

items.q: Which glass has the most water?
items.e: The glasses are the same size. Look for the highest water. Glass B is nearly full, so B has the most.

items.q: Each container is full. Which one holds the most?
items.e: B is the widest and as tall as C. C is tall but very thin. So B holds the most. Tall does not always mean it holds more.

items.q: Tunde pours all the cups into the jug. Now the jug is full. How many cups does the jug hold?
items.e: Count the cups: 1, 2, 3, 4. The jug holds 4 cups of water. Do not count the jug.

items.q: Which glass has the least water?
items.e: Look for the lowest water. Glass C is nearly empty. It has less than D, which is quarter full. So C has the least.

items.q: Which glass is half full?
items.e: Half full means the water comes up to the middle. Glass C is nearly full, not half full. D is half full.

items.q: Esther’s cup of milk is full. She drinks half of it. How full is the cup now?
items.e: Half the milk is gone. Half is left. The cup is half full.

items.q: Which glass is quarter full?
items.e: Quarter full means 1 of 4 equal parts has water. Glass B is half full. A is quarter full.

items.q: Which glass is full?
items.e: Full means the water comes right up to the top. A is nearly full, but there is a gap at the top. B is full.

items.q: Chidi pours all the cups into the jug. Now the jug is full. How many cups does the jug hold?
items.e: Count the cups: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. The jug holds 7 cups of water. Do not count the jug.

items.q: Each container is full. Which one holds the least?
items.e: C is the thinnest and the shortest. So C holds the least.

items.q: Which can hold more water?
items.e: A bucket is much bigger inside than a cup or a spoon. A bucket holds more.

items.q: A glass is half full. Kayode adds water until it is full. Is there more or less water now?
items.e: The water went up from the middle to the top. So there is more water now.
